quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-01.prompt:
Let $G$ be a finite group and fix a prime number $p$. Define the function $f$ on the set of subgroups $H \subseteq G$ by
$$f(H) = |\{ P \in \mathrm{Syl}_p(G) \mid P \supseteq H \}|.$$
In other words, $f(H)$ is the number of Sylow $p$-subgroups of $G$ which contain $H$. Prove that if $f(H) > 0$, then $f(H) \equiv 1 \bmod p$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-01.answer: Downward induction on $|H|$: a Sylow $p$-subgroup $T$ of $N_G(H)$ acts by conjugation on the Sylow subgroups containing $H$; the fixed points are exactly the Sylow subgroups containing $T$, and $T\supsetneq H$ unless $H$ is Sylow. So $f(H)\equiv f(T)\equiv1\pmod p$.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-02.prompt:
Let $F$ be a field and let $R$ be the ring of all $3 \times 3$ matrices over $F$ with $(3,1)$ and $(3,2)$ entry equal to $0$. Thus,
$$R = \begin{pmatrix} F & F & F \\ F & F & F \\ 0 & 0 & F \end{pmatrix}.$$
Prove that the Jacobson radical of $R$ is a minimal left ideal, but not a minimal right ideal.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-02.answer: $J(R)=J=\{$matrices supported on entries $(1,3),(2,3)\}$: $J^2=0$ and $R/J\cong M_2(F)\times F$ is semisimple. $J\cong F^2$ as a left module over the $M_2(F)$ block, which is simple; but the matrices supported on entry $(1,3)$ form a smaller nonzero right ideal.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-03.prompt:
Let $F$ be a field and let $f(x) \in F[x]$ be an irreducible polynomial. Suppose $E$ is a splitting field for $f(x)$ over $F$ and assume that there exists an element $\alpha \in E$ such that both $\alpha$ and $\alpha + 1$ are roots of $f(x)$.

(i) Show that the characteristic of $F$ is not zero.

(ii) Prove that there exists a field $L$ between $F$ and $E$ such that the degree $|E : L|$ is equal to the characteristic of $F$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-03.answer: There is $\sigma\in\mathrm{Aut}(E/F)$ with $\sigma(\alpha)=\alpha+1$, so $\alpha+k$ is a root for every $k$. (i) Finitely many roots force $\mathrm{char}F=p>0$. (ii) $\sigma$ has order divisible by $p$; take $\tau$ of order $p$ in $\mathrm{Aut}(E/F)$ and $L=E^{\langle\tau\rangle}$, so $|E:L|=p$ by Artin's theorem.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-04.prompt:
Let $V$ be a finite dimensional complex vector space and suppose $\langle\ ,\ \rangle\colon V \times V \to \mathbb{C}$ is an inner product on $V$, that is, $\langle\ ,\ \rangle$ is a positive definite Hermitian form on $V$.

(i) Suppose $T\colon V \to V$ is a linear transformation such that $\langle Tv, v\rangle = 0$ for all $v \in V$. Prove that $V = 0$. [*Sic*; the intended conclusion is $T = 0$.]

(ii) Does the result of part (i) hold if $V$ is assumed to be a real inner product space? Justify your answer.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-04.answer: (i) $T=0$: polarize, using $v+w$ and $v+iw$, to get $\langle Tv,w\rangle=0$ for all $v,w$. (ii) No: rotation by $90^\circ$ on $\mathbb R^2$ satisfies $\langle Tv,v\rangle=0$ but $T\ne0$.
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-04.reviewNote: The exam text says 'Prove that V = 0' in part (i); this is clearly a misprint for 'T = 0' (V need not be 0). Solution proves T = 0.

quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-05.prompt:
Let $\mathbb{Z}$ denote the ring of integers and let $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{C}$ be the rational and complex fields, respectively. If $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n \in \mathbb{C}$, then we let $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n]$ denote the ring generated by these elements over $\mathbb{Z}$. In particular, note that $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$ is the set of all rational numbers with denominator a power of $2$. Now suppose that $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n$ are the roots of the integer polynomial $f(x) = a_0x^n + a_1x^{n-1} + \cdots + a_n \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $a_0 = 2$.

(i) Prove that $2\alpha_i$ is an algebraic integer for all $i = 1, 2, \ldots, n$.

(ii) Show that $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n] \cap \mathbb{Q} \subseteq \mathbb{Z}[1/2]$.

(iii) If some $a_j$ with $j \ge 1$ is odd, prove that $1/2 \in \mathbb{Z}[\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n] \cap \mathbb{Q}$ and deduce that the latter intersection is equal to $\mathbb{Z}[1/2]$. What happens if all $a_j$ are even?
quals-wisconsin-algebra-1992s-05.answer: (i) $2\alpha_i$ is a root of the monic $x^n+a_1x^{n-1}+2a_2x^{n-2}+\dots+2^{n-1}a_n$. (ii) $2^N r$ is an algebraic integer for $r\in\mathbb Z[\alpha]$, so rational $r$ lie in $\mathbb Z[1/2]$. (iii) $a_j/2=\pm e_j(\alpha)\in\mathbb Z[\alpha]$, giving $1/2$; if all $a_j$ are even the $\alpha_i$ are algebraic integers and the intersection is $\mathbb Z$.
